target_claim: The forward direction of the reduction: grouping all four copies of the three elements of each 3-Partition block yields subsets that all have the same sum, so a yes-instance of 3-Partition maps to a yes-instance of 12Partition.
source_quote:
where Cj depends only on the indices. Since each index appears in exactly one partition set,
all Aj have the same sum.
test_sketch: Implement the reduction verbatim: for each ti in T build s(j)_i = ti + j*K*4^(3m+1-i), j=1..4, K=1+mB. Take the yes-instance m=2, T={5,5,5,5,5,5}, B=15 (satisfies B/4<ti<B/2 and a valid 3-partition exists). Build the two forward-direction subsets A1, A2 from any 3-partition and print their sums: they differ, because sum(Aj)=4B+10K*Cj with Cj = 4^(3m+1-i) summed over Aj's three distinct indices, and distinct powers of 4 give distinct Cj. Then brute-force over all C(24,12)/2 splits of S into two 12-element halves (an oracle over the 6-element 3-Partition input) to confirm NO equal-sum 12Partition of S exists at all, so the reduction maps a yes-instance to a no-instance, refuting the claimed equivalence.
